Would you rather have the cost of roads be paid by tolls or taxes?

Taxes.

It costs a lot of money to set up toll collection. So it would be cheaper to just get it from taxes. It has the disadvantage of taxing everyone equally rather than by usage, but even people who do not drive benefit from having a road system. So I am not too concerned.

Taxes. The majority of road infrastructure damage is directly caused by vehicles with more than 2 axles. Instituting taxes on the transportation industry to pay for that damage would be more than fair (either by vehicle miles traveled taxes or special vehicle taxes which could be collected at weigh stations). Additionally, special vehicle taxes will need to be implemented as electric cars become more prevalent, as the majority of roadwork is funded directly from the gasoline tax.

Toll roads only result in taking public funding out of the hands of greedy and corrupt politicians and placing it in the hands of greedy self-serving corporations. That would then generate a conflict of interest when it comes to law enforcement, as any police action on those private roads would then be being paid for by the public (assuming the police don't similarly end up privatized).

Can you elaborate more on the subscription idea?

ISP's charge for a connection from their infrastructure to your house. They then pay for connections to other companies' networks to get your traffic out to the larger internet.

Let's say you paid your local road maintenance provider for the construction of your driveway connecting your garage to the street. You and anyone else with a connection to the street pays a subscription fee based on the size of the connection or the expected level of usage. Businesses would pay more because they have larger volumes and heavier traffic than houses. They also are more likely to want to connect to more high traffic roads than smaller streets.

Different companies could operate in the same general area providing competition. It would be beneficial to them to connect their local roads to larger systems.
